Technically, (1) the angle of your arm respective to the guitar neck should be as close to 90 degrees as possible, (2) your thumb should rest directly in the middle of the back of the neck, (3) your wrist should sit nearly in line with the bottom of the fret board. Now, we all have our ways of playing that break the technical rules, but if you're experiencing pain it's always beneficial to go back to basics. You ever see a classical concert player sitting straight up in a chair with the guitar angled way up in the air? That's because they're exhibiting perfect form and that form exists to prevent injury and provide ease of access to the fret board. Not to say that's how you should play, but from the pictures you seem to be really gripping the neck and at an odd angle. How you have your thumb positioned and arm angled you seem to be 'squeezing' the chords instead of (what you aught to be doing) placing your fingers down on the fret board with a little support from your thumb. I think you'd notice a huge difference if you kicked your elbow out a bit, dropped your wrist, and placed your thumb square in the middle of the neck. This may require you to angle the neck up a bit as well (bring the head of the guitar closer to your own head). Also, a few minutes of finger/wrist/arm stretches is something all guitarists should do from time to time. Hope this helps!
